resumen: Three days a week alternating A and B at home, with nothing but the floor and a wall: squats, push-ups, bridges and core work. For getting started or for weeks without a gym.
matices: Without weights, progress comes differently: harder variations (from push-ups with hands on a table or wall to regular, then diamond; from two-leg to one-leg bridges) or longer holds in the timed exercises. A review found that muscle gain happens across a wide range of loads if sets are taken close to failure, so bodyweight works as long as each set gets close to failure within the range; once you pass the top, move to a harder variation. Without a bar or bands there is no way to train the back with a pulling movement; if you can, add a pull with equipment later. Reps for one-sided exercises are per side, and the numbers for the plank, superman and wall sit are seconds.
